correctness.rationale: Direct transition enumeration supplies exact birth and death rates. With 0<p<1 all rates joining adjacent states are positive, giving a unique symmetric stationary law. The exact ratio T(j) obeys T(j)>T(M-j) for 0<j<M/2 because the correction numerator is reflection symmetric and its denominator is increasing, yielding a monotone radial density ratio; convex order then follows by symmetrizing each convex test function. The case N=3 has equality; N≥4 has strict variance comparison. For q=3,N=4 the ratio T3(1)/T3(2)<1 reverses the ordering. The full proof is analytical, and an independently enumerated exact rational checker passed 6492 assertions; finite checks alone do not cover unbounded N.

value.rationale: The original influence-group sampling distinction affects sociological predictions. A parameter-uniform, all-population convex-order comparison quantifies its effect on every convex polarization metric and, with a smallest-admissible q3 reversal, establishes that the effect is structurally nonuniversal. The equality/strict population cutoff is exact, not a computational arbitrarily chosen invariant, and the result cannot be inferred from the infinite-population approximation where sampling schemes coincide.
